name: Traditional and folk religions
text: Local ancestral, animist and nature religions, passed on orally rather than through a scripture or church.

name: Tengrism
text: The sky-god religion of the Turkic and Mongol steppe peoples, with shamans as intermediaries.

name: Ancient Egyptian religion
text: The gods of the Nile with the pharaoh as divine king, centred on temples and the afterlife.

name: Mesopotamian and Canaanite religion
text: The city gods of Sumer, Babylon and Assyria and the related Canaanite and Phoenician cults of Baal and Astarte.

name: Greek and Roman religion
text: The Olympian gods of Greece and Rome, worshipped through civic temples, sacrifice and oracles, with the Roman emperor cult added later.

name: Celtic, Germanic, Norse and Slavic paganism
text: The pre-Christian religions of northern and eastern Europe: druids, Odin and Thor, Perun and the Baltic gods.

name: Mesoamerican religion
text: The temple-pyramid religions of the Olmec, Maya, Toltec and Aztec, with a shared calendar and gods like Quetzalcoatl.

name: Andean religion
text: The religions of Chavin, Moche, Tiwanaku and the Inca, centred on the sun god Inti, mountain spirits and ancestor mummies.

name: Judaism
text: The monotheism of the Israelites, centred on the Torah, first on the Jerusalem Temple and after AD 70 on rabbis and synagogues.

name: Zoroastrianism
text: Zarathustra's faith in the wise lord Ahura Mazda and the struggle of good against evil, state religion of three Persian empires.

name: Manichaeism
text: Mani's dualist religion of light and darkness, which spread from Persia to Rome and China and was state religion of the Uyghurs.

name: Vedic religion
text: The fire sacrifices and hymns of the Vedas, the root of Hinduism.

name: Hinduism
text: The family of traditions devoted to Vishnu, Shiva and the Goddess, built on the Vedas, the epics and temple worship.

name: Jainism
text: Mahavira's path of non-violence and asceticism.

name: Early Buddhism
text: The Buddha's teaching in its first Indian centuries, before the Theravada and Mahayana traditions separated.

name: Theravada Buddhism
text: The 'teaching of the elders', based on the Pali canon, followed in Sri Lanka, Burma, Thailand, Laos and Cambodia.

name: Mahayana Buddhism
text: The 'great vehicle' with its bodhisattvas and many sutras, including Chan or Zen and Pure Land, followed in China, Korea, Japan and Vietnam.

name: Tibetan (Vajrayana) Buddhism
text: Tantric Buddhism led by lamas such as the Dalai Lama, followed in Tibet, Mongolia, Bhutan and Buryatia.

name: Confucianism, Taoism and Chinese folk religion
text: China's blend of ancestor worship, Confucian ethics and Taoist practice, practised alongside Buddhism.

name: Shinto
text: Japan's worship of the kami at shrines, intertwined with Buddhism for a thousand years and made a state cult from 1868 to 1945.

name: Christianity (before the Great Schism)
text: The one imperial church of the Roman world, before Catholics and Orthodox split in 1054.

name: Arian Christianity
text: Christians who held that the Son was created by the Father; condemned at Nicaea in 325 but the faith of the Goths, Vandals and Lombards until about 700.

name: Oriental Orthodoxy (Coptic, Ethiopian, Armenian, Syriac)
text: The ancient churches that rejected the Council of Chalcedon in 451: the Coptic, Ethiopian, Eritrean, Armenian and Syriac Orthodox churches.

name: Church of the East (Nestorian)
text: The Persian church whose missionaries reached India, Central Asia and Tang China.

name: Roman Catholicism
text: The Latin church led by the Pope in Rome, after the 1054 split with the Orthodox East.

name: Eastern Orthodoxy
text: The Greek, Slavic and Romanian churches in communion with Constantinople, after the 1054 split with Rome.

name: Hussite (Utraquist) Christianity
text: The Bohemian reform church of Jan Hus's followers, a century before Luther, which gave the laity the communion cup.

name: Lutheranism
text: The first Protestant church, from Martin Luther's break with Rome, dominant in northern Germany and Scandinavia.

name: Anglicanism
text: The Church of England, separated from Rome by Henry VIII in 1534, and its daughter churches across the British Empire.

name: Reformed (Calvinist and Presbyterian)
text: John Calvin's Protestantism: the Swiss, Dutch, Scottish Presbyterian and Huguenot churches.

name: Evangelical Protestantism
text: Later Protestant movements such as Baptists, Methodists and Pentecostals, strongest in the United States, Africa and Latin America today.

name: Sunni Islam
text: The majority branch of Islam, which accepted the elected caliphs as Muhammad's successors.

name: Twelver Shia Islam
text: The branch that follows Ali and twelve imams as Muhammad's rightful successors, state religion of Iran since 1501.

name: Ismaili Shia Islam
text: The Sevener branch of Shia Islam, faith of the Fatimid caliphs who ruled Egypt and North Africa from 909 to 1171.

name: Ibadi Islam
text: A small early branch of Islam, distinct from both Sunni and Shia, majority in Oman.

name: Sikhism
text: Guru Nanak's monotheist faith of the Punjab, whose Sikh Empire ruled the region from 1799 to 1849.

name: Secular or state atheism
text: Communist states that suppressed religion, and societies where most people now follow none.
